extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (mathematicians, computational number theorists, GP script authors and interactive users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and reference for interacting with the PARI/GP calculator: understanding error messages, debugging with break loop and iferr, customizing defaults and preferences, using readline and metacommands, interfacing with other languages, and the conventions used in the function reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parser error messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Parser messages indicate unexpected end-of-input and list expected continuations (e.g. ")-> or ',' or ')'"), showing what token the parser expected and where input ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual explains that when the parser reaches end-of-input it reports the tokens it would have accepted next; sometimes the message lists continuations that are syntactically possible but semantically odd (e.g. allowing an inline closure '(x)->sin(x)'). The caret pointing shows the location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime evaluator error messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Runtime errors from the evaluator report evaluation-time failures (e.g. undefined function called) with a caret pointing to the failing token and an explanatory message such as "not a function in function call".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runtime errors occur after successful parsing/compilation; messages identify the failing operation (e.g. siN vs sin) and show the expression and caret location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library runtime errors with mathematical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Library/runtime errors include the operator or library function name and explain the mathematical cause (e.g. "_/_: impossible inverse in Fp_inv: Mod(2,4)."), and provide deeper call-chain context when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the error is deeper in the call chain the debugger prints frames like 'in function g: ...' and 'in function f: ...' to help locate the origin. The surrounding context shows which operator/library function raised the error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-stack/frame reporting in error traces
rubrics_metrics.description: When an error occurs inside nested user functions or loops, gp reports enclosed frames (innermost first) showing the top-level, function bodies and loop frames that existed at the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trace shows lines like 'in function g: for(i=-N,N,f(i))' and 'in function f: 1/x' with carets indicating positions; loop bodies define extra frames and lexically scoped variables are available in their frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break loop behavior and entry conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A break loop is entered on Control-C (user interrupt) or a runtime/library/user error (not syntax errors), freezing gp state and presenting a 'break>' prompt for interactive inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inside break>, gp accepts gp commands (with history if using readline) and does not terminate on further errors. If break loop started by Control-C, an empty line resumes the computation; if started by a fatal error, empty line does nothing to avoid losing debugging data. Exit with next, break, return, or C-d (C-d twice may exit shell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using break loop to inspect and modify state
rubrics_metrics.description: While in a break loop you can inspect variables (including lexically-scoped ones preserved in frames), evaluate gp commands, change state (increase debug level, set variables, start logging) and then resume or abort the computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show typing variable names to print values, and modifying gp's state before continuing. The break loop prints the standard error message first and then the 'break>' prompt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging commands available in break loop
rubrics_metrics.description: dbg_up(n), dbg_down(n), dbg_x(t), dbg_err() are available to navigate frames, examine objects, and retrieve the current error context t_ERROR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: dbg_up goes up n frames, dbg_down cancels dbg_up, dbg_x is like \x but more flexible, and dbg_err() returns a t_ERROR object whose components can be inspected (e.g. Vec(ERR)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugger default and non-interactive behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The debugger (break loop) is enabled by default; it can be disabled by setting the default 'breakloop' to 0 in gprc. In non-interactive mode (stdin not a terminal) the break loop is automatically disabled and a runtime error simply sends you back to the prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a PARI stack overflow starts a break loop, the PARI stack is reset so commands can run; otherwise the stack would immediately overflow again. Disabling break loop changes runtime error behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: iferr: basic protected evaluation form
rubrics_metrics.description: iferr(statements, ERR, recovery) evaluates statements and returns its value unless an error occurs, in which case recovery is returned and ERR is a lexically-scoped variable set by the exception handler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: statements are partially evaluated and may have side effects. The ERR parameter helps the recovery code decide how to handle the error.

rubrics_metrics.name: iferr with predicate and selective trapping
rubrics_metrics.description: iferr(statements, ERR, recovery, predicate) only catches the exception if predicate is non-zero, enabling selective trapping based on ERR (e.g. errname(ERR) == "e_INV").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended practice: only trap errors of a specific kind; rethrow unexpected errors with error(ERR). Examples: inv2 that traps division-by-zero and rethrows type errors, and the simplified inv3.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERR object contents and inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERR formal parameter (a t_ERROR object) contains data beyond the error name; components accessible by component(ERR,1), component(ERR,2), ... or Vec(ERR), and errname(ERR) returns the error name string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the components to make fine-grained decisions in recovery code. See Section 3.11.17 for the list of exception types and contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using iferr to build fault-tolerant functions (example patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical pattern: try computation in statements, return recovery on expected error type, rethrow for unexpected types, or use predicate to only catch the desired exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: inv(x) = iferr(1/x, ERR, "oo") and inv2/ inv3 illustrating checking errname(ERR) and rethrowing with error(ERR) when the error is not expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using iferr for staged recovery/retry strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: iferr enables recovery strategies like restarting part of a computation at higher precision or attempting alternate computations when an anticipated error arises (e.g. lazy factorization revealing a factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual suggests using iferr to implement retry or fallback logic rather than letting the program terminate and lose intermediate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfacing GP with C and other languages
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI library is intended to be interfaced with C; gp provides convenient scripting for prototyping; install imports foreign functions for use under gp; GP2C can ease transition to C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: test and debug algorithms in gp scripts for simplicity and robustness, then code performance-critical parts in C if needed. Known external interfaces include SAGE (Python), Math::Pari (Perl), and a CLISP integration; these are third-party and not endorsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defaults mechanism and default(def, value) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use default(def, value) to set internal gp defaults; typing default by itself lists all defaults and current values. Defaults are often set once (colors, prompt) or used interactively (timer, precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default names in manual include initial values in parentheses; the second argument is subject to string context expansion (run-time values can be concatenated into the string).

rubrics_metrics.name: String context expansion and numeric suffixes in defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Second argument to default supports string context expansion (e.g. default(logfile, "file" a ".log")). Numeric suffixes k, M, G can be appended to numeric arguments to multiply by 10^3, 10^6, 10^9 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case-insensitive suffixes (30k or 30K). Some defaults corresponding to filenames or prompts also perform time expansion and environment variable expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and environment expansions for certain defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Some defaults (prompt, psfile, logfile) are subjected to time expansion via strftime (e.g. %H, %M) and environment expansion for $VARNAME and ~ home directory expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: default(prompt,"(%H:%M) ? ") prepends the time; environment expansion replaces $HOME or ~ with actual paths at the time they are set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferences file (gprc) purpose and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: gprc is gp's preferences file read at startup to customize defaults, load common user functions/aliases; explicit command-line switches override gprc values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gprc doesn't exist gp proceeds with initialization; the gprc file is processed before user interaction and after initializing defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: gprc file syntax and allowed constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: gprc is read line by line with comments removed and supports multiline constructions using braces, \, or =. Two preprocessor-style constructs are special: lines starting with #if boolean used as conditional comments; after preprocessing only two kinds of expressions are recognized: default = value and read "some GP file".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes for strings; read delays file input until gprc fully loaded. Example shows conditional blocks using #if VERSION > 2.2.3 and #if EMACS.

rubrics_metrics.name: gprc preprocessor conditionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines starting with '#if boolean' are treated as comments if boolean evaluates to false, otherwise read normally; tests available: EMACS, READL (readline), and 'VERSION op number' where op is >, <, <=, or >=.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The directive applies to the current line; if rest of line is empty the test applies to next line. Negation allowed (#if not or #if !).

rubrics_metrics.name: gprc lookup order / location
rubrics_metrics.description: When gp starts it looks for gprc in this order: file named by $GPRC, $HOME/.gprc (Unix) or $HOME\gprc.txt (Windows), /etc/gprc (system-wide), and finally pari's datadir (.gprc or gprc.txt). Only the first found is loaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Unix the default user gprc is hidden (starts with .); use ls -a to view it. Environment variable GPRC can be used to point to a custom file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple metacommands: purpose and script-use prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple metacommands (mostly starting with \) are shortcuts for interactive use and should not be used in GP scripts. They are case sensitive and braces denote optional args with defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitespace between metacommand and arguments is optional (can cause problems for some commands). Example: \Q, \q are distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online help metacommands (? , ?? , ??? )
rubrics_metrics.description: ?n lists functions in Section 3.n; ?function gives short explanation; ?? keyword yields the function description as in the manual and supports operators and chapter selection (using @n); ??? pattern lists sections of Chapter 3 related to query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes for queries containing dangerous characters. ?? without argument opens a dvi previewer of the manual. ??tutorial and ??refcard open tutorial and reference card previews. Extended help requires perl/gphelp installation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Block comments: /* ... */ span lines and are ignored. One-line comments: \\ (backslash-backslash) cause the rest of the line to be ignored by gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comment syntaxes apply generally; multiline comments are recognized in gprc too.

rubrics_metrics.name: \a metacommand: raw object printing
rubrics_metrics.description: \a {n} prints the object number n (%n) in raw format; if n omitted prints latest computed object (%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to inspect internal representation of history objects in raw form.

rubrics_metrics.name: \c metacommand: list hardcoded functions
rubrics_metrics.description: \c prints the list of all available hardcoded functions under gp, excluding operators written as special symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information about functions can be obtained with ?function. For user-defined functions/member functions see \u and \um.

rubrics_metrics.name: \d metacommand: print defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: \d prints the defaults (shortcut for default()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows available defaults and their current values.

rubrics_metrics.name: \e metacommand: echo mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \e {n} switches echo mode on (1) or off (0); if n omitted, toggles or prints current state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control whether commands are echoed as they execute.

rubrics_metrics.name: \g metacommand: set debugging level
rubrics_metrics.description: \g {n} sets the debugging level debug to non-negative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to control general debugging verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: \gf metacommand: set file usage debugging level
rubrics_metrics.description: \gf {n} sets debugfiles to non-negative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for file-related debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: \gm metacommand: set memory debugging level
rubrics_metrics.description: \gm {n} sets debugmem to non-negative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to debug memory-related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: \h metacommand: hashtable debugging/info
rubrics_metrics.description: \h {m-n} outputs debugging info about the hashtable; a single number n outputs cell n; m-n prints a range; a function name prints internal structure of that hash cell; '-' prints statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for low-level debugging and inspecting internal hash structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: \l metacommand: logging control
rubrics_metrics.description: \l {logfile} switches log mode on/off; if logfile given, sets the default logfile and turns logging on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to start/stop session logging; related to default logfile setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: \m metacommand: prettymatrix print
rubrics_metrics.description: \m prints the object %n but using prettymatrix format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like \a but in prettier matrix form.

rubrics_metrics.name: \o metacommand: set output mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \o {n} sets output mode (0 raw, 1 prettymatrix, 3 external prettyprint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls how gp displays results.

rubrics_metrics.name: \p metacommand: set precision
rubrics_metrics.description: \p {n} sets realprecision to n decimal digits; prints current value if n omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to change default numeric precision interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ps metacommand: set series precision
rubrics_metrics.description: \ps {n} sets seriesprecision to n significant terms; prints current value if n omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls precision for series expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: \q metacommand: quit session
rubrics_metrics.description: \q quits the gp session and returns to the system (shortcut for quit()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to exit gp interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: \r metacommand: read file into gp
rubrics_metrics.description: \r {filename} reads all commands from filename as if typed from keyboard; if filename omitted re-reads previously used input file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a gp binary file is read it is silently loaded; accepts compressed files (.Z, .gz, .z) and decompresses on the fly. Note: \r stores history entry per input line, different from read() function.

rubrics_metrics.name: \s metacommand: PARI stack/heap state
rubrics_metrics.description: \s prints the state of the PARI stack and heap for debugging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily a developer/debugging tool to inspect PARI memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: \t metacommand: internal format display
rubrics_metrics.description: \t prints internal longword format of all PARI types; detailed bit/byte format covered in Chapter 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for low-level inspection of internal representations; typical gp users need not know the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: \u and \um metacommands: user-defined functions
rubrics_metrics.description: \u prints definitions of all user-defined functions; \um prints definitions of all user-defined member functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helpful to inspect functions you defined during a session.

rubrics_metrics.name: \v metacommand: version info
rubrics_metrics.description: \v prints the version number and implementation architecture (e.g. 680x0, Sparc, Alpha) of the gp executable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to determine which gp build you are running.

rubrics_metrics.name: \w metacommand: write object to file
rubrics_metrics.description: \w {n} {filename} writes object number n (%n) into named file in raw format; if n omitted writes latest object; if filename omitted appends to logfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underlying write() is more powerful for arbitrary filenames; \w is a convenience for basic raw dumps.

rubrics_metrics.name: \x metacommand: print complete internal tree
rubrics_metrics.description: \x {n} prints the complete tree with addresses and hexadecimal contents of internal representation of object n (%n); if n omitted uses latest object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly used for debugging; dbg_x is a more versatile underlying function.

rubrics_metrics.name: \y metacommand: toggle simplify
rubrics_metrics.description: \y {n} switches simplify on (1) or off (0); if n given sets simplify to n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls automatic simplification behavior of printed results.

rubrics_metrics.name: # and ## metacommands: timer toggle and last time
rubrics_metrics.description: # toggles the timer on/off; ## prints time taken by latest computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for ad-hoc timing; remember to turn timer on before long computations if you want the timing shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacommand \o and completion interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: When Tab completes defaults it will append an ending comma; when completing a function name it appends parentheses and a second Tab will show argument list as given by online help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion is context-dependent and may add a comma or parentheses automatically to save keystrokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using readline: line editing and history
rubrics_metrics.description: Readline provides line editing, history (multiline commands stored as a single concatenated line), incremental search (C-r/C-s), movement (C-a/C-e, M-b/M-f), kill/yank, undo, transpose and Vi mode toggle (M-C-j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readline keybindings can be customized in .inputrc; C-x C-r rereads the init file. Meta key may be Alt or Esc depending on system.

rubrics_metrics.name: .inputrc customization for gp
rubrics_metrics.description: Create .inputrc in home directory to change readline bindings and behavior for gp; example shows conditional $if Pari-GP and custom bindings (e.g. show-all-if-ambiguous, custom key sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C-x C-r re-reads .inputrc during a session. Use bindings to tune behavior like backward-delete-char or to avoid interfering with copy-paste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electric parentheses and pari-matched-insert
rubrics_metrics.description: By default '(' and '[' are bound to pari-matched-insert which, when 'electric parentheses' is enabled (default off), automatically inserts the matching closure ')' or ']' and can be toggled with numeric arguments (M--2 to toggle, M--0/M--1 to explicitly off/on).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electric insertion is useful but may interfere with copy-paste; toggle as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readline completion and online help
rubrics_metrics.description: TAB performs context-dependent completion; if only one completion is meaningful gp inserts it plus context-specific endings (comma for defaults, parentheses for functions). Hitting TAB again lists possible completions. M-h shows short online help for the word under the cursor; M-H shows extended help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion uses gp's knowledge of defaults, filenames, functions, operators, member keywords, etc. Example: def<TAB>se<TAB>10 expands to default(seriesprecision,10).

rubrics_metrics.name: PariEmacs integration (using PariEmacs package)
rubrics_metrics.description: PariEmacs lets you run gp as a subprocess in GNU Emacs; add autoload lines for gp-mode and gp-script-mode to .emacs and associate .gp files with gp-script-mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once set up, M-x gp starts a special shell launching gp; you get Emacs editor facilities while interacting with gp. See PariEmacs docs for menus and customizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function documentation and argument-convention conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Function entries are documented with syntax like foo(x, {flag = 0}): short description. '{}' denotes optional arguments; {}* denotes any number of such arguments. Commas or closing parenthesis can signal using defaults (foo(x,) accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional arguments are placed at end in order of decreasing usefulness; the 'empty arg' trick foo(6,,1) allows skipping middle defaults. A function with no mandatory arguments may be invoked without parentheses as a standalone name (not recommended for scripts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flags: meaning and documentation convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Flags are optional arguments that change default behavior (e.g. return more/less information); the manual distinguishes flag kinds and documents valid values (e.g. 'If flag is equal to 1, then...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags are described per-function in the reference; they are optional and intended to alter output verbosity/behavior rather than convey primary data.
